paragraphs: Feitian means flying apsara, a figure from Buddhist cave painting, and the name was chosen deliberately for the suit China built for spacewalks. It is a rear entry design with a rigid torso, and the first time it was used outside a spacecraft it made China the third country to have done so.

The figure holds 60,597 polygons and 63,640 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 17 maps, 16 at 4096x4096 and one at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits space programme visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum and education work, film, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A camera dolly is a machine for removing the operator's footsteps from a shot. Everything about it, the levelling, the arm, the wheels that steer in several modes, exists so the camera moves and nothing else does. Loaded with a compact large format body, it is the standard rig on a working set.
The model holds 523,706 polygons and 278,623 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the dolly together with the camera. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits film and broadcast production visualisation, equipment marketing, studio and set scenes, previsualisation, education and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

An observation tower is a building whose only product is the view. The shaft is structure, the platform is the point, and the whole thing is designed to be looked at from the city as much as looked out from, which is why so many of them end up on postcards.
The model holds 141,448 polygons and 167,944 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, suited to the repeated structure, and carries StemCell certification.
At $129 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, tourism imagery, city skyline scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Colonial style is symmetry with a door in the middle: shutters either side, a central hall behind, and a roofline that has barely changed in two centuries of American building. Adding a garage is the modern concession, and it is usually where the symmetry breaks.
The model holds 517,083 polygons and 512,926 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the house and its attached garage. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits architectural and residential visualisation, property marketing, suburban scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Premium saloons converged on one shape a long time ago, and beige is the colour that admits it. The car is meant to be unremarkable in the best sense: correct proportions, no statement, and a presence that suits a driveway or a hotel forecourt without drawing attention.

The model holds 257,665 polygons and 278,292 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the wheels and doors can be posed. It carries StemCell certification, and the library also holds a simplified build for background use.
At $129 it suits architectural and street visualisation, automotive marketing, advertising, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Older people in renders are almost always shown sitting, walking slowly or needing something. A party dress is a corrective: the same figure dressed for an evening out, which is a far more accurate picture of how most people actually spend their seventies.

The figure is light at 10,848 polygons and 11,687 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 17 maps, 13 at 4096x4096, one at 3000x3000 and 3 at 1000x1000. It is supplied in a T pose ready for your own rig and carries StemCell certification.
At $129 it suits architectural and interior visualisation, advertising and lifestyle imagery, event and hospitality scenes, game crowds and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Delivery is the use case electric trucks were always going to win first: fixed routes, predictable mileage, and a depot to charge at overnight. A cab over body with a short wheelbase is the shape that does most of that work in cities.
The model holds 650,194 polygons and 662,130 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $129 it suits logistics and fleet visualisation, electric vehicle presentation, livery mockups, street and architectural scenes, advertising and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Etihad Towers is a group rather than a building, and the arrangement is the point: five curved shafts of different heights, leaning slightly, so the cluster reads as one composition from the Abu Dhabi corniche. It has appeared in enough films to be recognisable well beyond the Gulf.
The model holds 538,282 polygons and 691,008 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $129 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, tourism and property imagery, skyline scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

The Raptor was designed to be seen as late as possible and never exported, which makes it one of the few modern fighters no other air force flies. The faceted intakes and the alignment of every edge on the airframe are all consequences of that single requirement.

The airframe holds 388,102 polygons and 393,152 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 8 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and news graphics, film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

The MiG-35 is the last development of a design that first flew in the Cold War, updated with new radar, new engines and a glass cockpit. Whether that counts as a new fighter or an old one wearing new equipment is an argument that has followed the aircraft since it appeared.

The airframe holds 109,083 polygons and 120,674 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 27 maps, 3 at 8192x8192, 15 at 2048x2048, 8 at 1024x1024 and one at 512x512. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and news graphics, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

Air taxi concepts are the aviation industry arguing with itself in public. The Nexus 6HX is one answer: ducted rotors rather than exposed blades, a cabin sized for a car's worth of passengers, and a design that has to be quiet enough for a city to tolerate before it can be fast.
The model holds 214,052 polygons and 109,964 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $129 it suits future mobility visualisation, technology and transport presentation, advertising, science fiction film, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A tow truck arrives when something has already gone wrong, which is why it appears in so many scenes as a narrative device rather than as a vehicle. The medium duty chassis is the sweet spot: heavy enough to lift a car, small enough to work a city street.

The model holds 557,548 polygons and 563,125 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 20 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits street and architectural visualisation, roadside assistance and fleet presentation, advertising, film and television, and game environments. On sale since 2020.

A generic SUV is often more useful than a specific one. No badge means no licensing question, no dating of the image, and no client asking why a competitor's car is parked outside their building. It reads as a car and nothing more, which is exactly the job.

The model holds 268,207 polygons and 284,155 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 30 maps, 13 at 4096x4096, 16 at 2048x2048 and one at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $129 it suits architectural and street visualisation, advertising and mockup work, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

Baling solved storage, and then created a handling problem. A bale wagon is the answer: it picks up, stacks and carries in one pass, so a field can be cleared before the weather changes without anyone lifting anything by hand.

The model holds 264,236 polygons and 296,847 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and comes rigged so the wagon and its mechanism can be posed or animated. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $129 it suits agricultural machinery marketing, farming visualisation, rural scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.
